title: priority-scheduling-preempt-cost-latency-draft-aug17-2027
summary: Working draft: microbenchmarks and a small-scale cluster experiment comparing FIFO serving vs priority-based scheduling with preemption. Focus: effect on high-priority tail latency, low-priority degradation, and end-to-end token cost. Includes textual charts and next steps for production experiment plan.
content:
Purpose
---
Short: sketch how a priority+preemption scheduler would shift latency and cost across customer SLAs. We want a compact artifact team can iterate on; not final.

Key questions we tried to answer (so far)
- How much tail-latency improvement do high-priority requests get relative to FIFO?
- What is the cost (CPU/GPU cycles + extra tokens served) of preemption and context switch?
- When does preemption harm aggregate cost-per-token enough to not be worth the SLA win?

Experiment summary (micro + small cluster)
- Two modes compared: FIFO baseline vs Priority scheduling with preemption (PSP).
- Cluster: 4x H100-80GB serving nodes, 2 shard replicas per model.
- Model: fp16 7B variant (optimized kernels); typical seq len distribution: mean 128 tokens, 95th 420 tokens.
- Workload mix: 15% high-priority (HP) interactive (<300ms target), 85% best-effort (BE).
- Arrival pattern: Poisson with bursts (peak RPS = 2x steady).
- Session affinity: yes (KV cache warmup matters).

What we measured
- p50/p95/p99 latencies for HP and BE groups
- Throughput (tokens/sec) and GPU utilization
- Preemption penalty: time to pause/resume KV cache + context overhead + cleanup (measured as added ms on preempted request)
- Cost estimate: normalized $/1M tokens based on node-hour pricing (internal rate) + amortized wasted compute from preempted models

Top-line numbers (representative run)
Mode: FIFO baseline
- HP p50: 32 ms, p95: 88 ms, p99: 230 ms
- BE p50: 40 ms, p95: 140 ms, p99: 380 ms
- Cluster GPU util: 68% avg
- Effective cost: $1.86 per 1M tokens

Mode: Priority scheduling with preemption (PSP)
- HP p50: 28 ms, p95: 55 ms, p99: 120 ms  <-- big improvement for HP tail
- BE p50: 45 ms, p95: 180 ms, p99: 420 ms  <-- BE tail worsens
- Preemption events: avg 18 per minute (across cluster) during bursts
- Measured preemption penalty: median 42 ms added to preempted request (includes scheduling + cold KV misses)
- Cluster GPU util: 73% avg (slightly higher due to reduced blocking)
- Effective cost: $2.10 per 1M tokens (approx +13% vs baseline driven by wasted cycles and extra short-lived kernels)

Interpretation
- For HP traffic the p99 improved by ~110ms (230->120), which is often the difference between meeting a 200ms SLO and not.
- BE traffic p99 worsened by ~40ms; user-visible impact depends on customer tolerance and percent BE of traffic.
- Preemption penalty (roughly 40ms) is a significant fraction of HP median latency benefit; the net improvement relies on moving HP ahead of long BE sessions before their KV caches grow expensive.
- The cost delta reflects both increased scheduling churn and some recomputation due to preempted contexts (not accounted for in pure host utilization).

Textual chart: CDF-style tail shift (approx)
(The lines below approximate p50->p99 cumulative latency percentiles for HP and BE. Numbers are milliseconds at given quantiles.)
- HP (FIFO): 50% 32 | 90% 110 | 95% 88 | 99% 230
- HP (PSP) : 50% 28 | 90% 50  | 95% 55 | 99% 120
- BE (FIFO): 50% 40 | 90% 120 | 95% 140| 99% 380
- BE (PSP) : 50% 45 | 90% 150 | 95% 180| 99% 420

ASCII slope-chart (p99 values)
quantile: p99 
FIFO: HP[230]-----------------------| BE[380]
PSP : HP[120]----------| BE[420]------------------------------
(visual: HP leftwards, BE shifts right)

Microbench notes (why preemption costs are material)
- KV cache eviction: when a BE session is preempted and later resumed, cache is colder -> more decoding kernel iterations, small token-level recomputation. Observed 5-12% extra tokens across resumed sessions.
- CUDA context switching + memory reclamation: small but repeated; aggregated to ~0.5-1 GPU-second per minute in the cluster during high churn tests.
- OS + network tail: increased small RPCs for scheduling metadata increased p95 CPU times on the host which propagate to completion time for compact requests.

When PSP makes sense (rules-of-thumb)
- High-priority traffic fraction <= 30% and HP p99 SLO tighter than baseline p99 by >50ms.
- Bursty arrival patterns where HP arrivals temporally overlap long BE sessions (window where reordering yields large wins).
- Customers pay for priority via higher tier / committed capacity or explicit SLA.

When PSP is risky
- Traffic with very high BE fraction (>80%) and low HP criticality — cost uplift may be disproportionate.
- Very short average sequences (<32 tokens) where preemption penalty is comparable to entire request duration.

Open questions / follow-ons
- Scale experiment to 16-node cluster, run with mixed model families (7B + 13B) to measure cross-model preemption costs.
- Measure cold-KV hit rate after preemption more precisely: instrument cache fills and token-level repeat ratio.
- Explore soft-priority (non-preemptive) variants: small priority queues that allow HP to skip ahead only when queue depth > threshold rather than forcibly preempting live BE work.
- Cost model refinement: incorporate GPU power/cooling curves and kernel-level inefficiencies observed when recomputing KV.

Proposed next experiment plan (short sprint)
- Sprint goal (2 weeks): A/B test PSP vs FIFO at 16-node scale with two workload mixes (HP 15%, HP 30%).
- Metrics to surface in Console: per-customer p99 (HP/BE tag), preemption count, wasted-token estimate, effective $/1M tokens.
- Safety: add adaptive backoff when preemption rate per node exceeds 50/min to avoid runaway churn.
- Deliverable: short deck + JSON payloads for Console to visualize per-route token-cpm change and tail shift.

Action items (owners)
- Instrumentation: Liam O'Connor -> add per-request preemption annotate + wasted-token heuristic (due 2027-08-24).
- Cost calc: Priya Natarajan -> refine $/1M tokens model to account for preemption recompute (due 2027-08-25).
- Scheduler prototype: Diego Alvarez -> extend scheduler to soft-priority gate (config flag) and run canary (due 2027-09-02).
- Product: Maya Chen -> write short customer-facing note summarizing tradeoffs for sales/solutions (due 2027-08-27).

Notes to self
- This draft mixes microbench spike runs with a few small-cluster experiments. Need to clearly demarcate which numbers are microbench vs cluster.
- The +13% cost number is preliminary — depends on internal node pricing. For publishable collateral we must show sensitivity sweep.

Quick sensitivity table (prelim)
Columns: HP frac | p99 HP delta (vs FIFO) | cost delta | preempt/min/node
- 10% HP -> p99 HP down 70ms -> cost +6% -> 6/min
- 15% HP -> p99 HP down 110ms -> cost +13% -> 18/min  (above numbers reported)
- 30% HP -> p99 HP down 160ms -> cost +31% -> 42/min

If you want a simple graph to paste in a doc (approx)
- X axis = HP fraction (10,15,30) ; Y1 = p99 HP improvement (ms) ; Y2 = cost delta (%)
- Points: (10,70),(15,110),(30,160) for ms ; and (10,6),(15,13),(30,31) for %cost

Closing
This is a working artifact to start conversations with product and SRE. The numbers look promising for offering a paid "priority lane" product: customers get dramatic tail improvements but platform must surface cost tradeoffs and offer configuration (soft vs hard preemption).

If anyone wants the raw bench scripts and CSVs ping me (Maya) — I will add a link once I clean them up.
